clue.text: Roman claim to book ownership on 21

definitions.text: Roman claim to book ownership on 21

parts.words: Roman claim to book ownership on 21
parts.note: a Latin (Roman) phrase meaning 'from the books of', printed on the label at 21 to show who owns a volume

explanation.definitionFit: The Latin formula, meaning 'from the library of', is the standard owner's inscription on a pasted label inside a book's cover.

clue.text: Not quite Dante's. More Mamet's

parts.note: Edmond is the first name of Dumas's hero Dantès and the title of a David Mamet play; the wanted title, Thackeray's novel, differs from it by one letter

explanation.walkthrough: Dante here is not the poet: Edmond Dantès is the Count of Monte Cristo, and Edmond is a Mamet play. Change one letter of that name to reach Thackeray's historical novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Thackeray's novel about Henry of that name is a near-twin of the name Edmond shared by the Dumas hero and the Mamet play.

clue.text: Student on old vessel, fashionable poet

parts.note: L, the learner plate, stands for a student
Noah's ark is the famous ancient vessel
in means fashionable, as in 'the in thing'

explanation.surface: A trendy poet who once studied aboard an ancient ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Philip Larkin was an English poet, author of The Whitsun Weddings.

clue.text: Old monarchy supports refreshment in Elijah's refuge

indicators.note: in a down clue the supporting piece sits underneath, so the kingdom comes after the drink

parts.note: beer is a refreshing drink
Sheba was the ancient kingdom ruled by its famous queen

explanation.surface: An ancient kingdom keeps a prophet's hideaway stocked with drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: In 1 Kings 19 the prophet flees from Jezebel to this town in southern Judah before going into the wilderness.

clue.text: Cinemas run an odd version of Bennett work

indicators.note: an odd version is a strange rearrangement, telling us to reorder the letters of the words before it

explanation.surface: Picture houses are showing a peculiar adaptation of an Alan Bennett piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan Bennett wrote the television play The Insurance Man, about Kafka's work at a Prague insurance office.

clue.text: Gradation in German

parts.note: the German-coined linguistic term for vowel gradation, as in sing, sang, sung

explanation.definitionFit: The term names the systematic change of root vowel in related word forms, studied first in German grammar.

clue.text: Grave Scots poet, of premier significance

definitions.meaning: Robert ..., eighteenth-century Scottish poet, wrote the long poem The Grave
Tony ... was the UK prime minister (premier), so the surname is significant among premiers

explanation.definitionFit: The surname belongs both to the Scottish author of The Grave and to a British prime minister.

clue.text: American publisher in academy? In fact for younger readers

definitions.text: American publisher in academy? In fact for younger readers

parts.words: American publisher in academy? In fact for younger readers
parts.note: the New York publisher takes its name from a word for an academy or literary club, and runs a well-known imprint for young readers

explanation.definitionFit: Atheneum Books is a US publishing house whose name is the American spelling of athenaeum, a learned institution; it has a Books for Young Readers imprint.

clue.text: Walter 6 wrote one about America. A legendary history

definitions.text: Walter 6 wrote one about America. A legendary history

parts.words: Walter 6 wrote one about America. A legendary history
parts.note: Walter Blair (6 supplies the surname) wrote a 1944 book whose subtitle is A Legendary History of Our Humorous Heroes

explanation.definitionFit: A yarn of exaggerated exploits is the folk form Walter Blair's book collects, from Paul Bunyan to Davy Crockett.

clue.text: Apollo loved her as Mrs Ape, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps signals that the words before it are one possible arrangement of the letters wanted

explanation.surface: A woman a god adored, perhaps known as Mrs Ape.
explanation.walkthrough: In myth Apollo and Idas both wooed Marpessa, and Zeus let her choose; she chose the mortal Idas.
explanation.definitionFit: She is the daughter of Evenus whom the god Apollo desired and tried to carry off.

clue.text: A Clockwork Orange seen by him as synthetic

definitions.text: A Clockwork Orange seen by him as synthetic

parts.words: A Clockwork Orange seen by him as synthetic
parts.note: the pop artist filmed Burgess's novel in 1965 under the title Vinyl, a synthetic material

explanation.definitionFit: Andy Warhol's film Vinyl is a loose adaptation of A Clockwork Orange, and vinyl is a plastic.

clue.text: Dickensian character well suited by dolly varden

definitions.text: Dickensian character well suited by dolly varden

parts.words: Dickensian character well suited by dolly varden
parts.note: in Barnaby Rudge Dolly Varden is the companion of a young lady of the Warren; a dolly varden is also a flowered dress style named after her

explanation.definitionFit: Emma Haredale is the heroine of Dickens's Barnaby Rudge, whom Dolly Varden attends.

clue.text: Initially not an interesting literary subject at our fingertips

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the plural noun: what we find at the ends of our fingers

indicators.note: initially means taking the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A dull literary topic, though readily to hand.
explanation.definitionFit: Fingernails grow at the very tips of the fingers.

clue.text: Night watchman?

parts.note: not a guard but the painter of the Dutch masterpiece The Night Watch

explanation.definitionFit: The Dutch painter created The Night Watch, the militia group portrait in the Rijksmuseum.

clue.text: Proust character sort of a lean Justine

indicators.note: sort of tells us the following words are to be sorted into a new order

explanation.surface: A Proustian figure who is roughly a slimmer Justine.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Santeuil is the hero of Proust's early, unfinished autobiographical novel of that name.

clue.text: Pomfret's preference

parts.note: John Pomfret's best-known poem, describing the life he would prefer, has a title meaning a preference

explanation.definitionFit: Pomfret's 1700 poem sets out his ideal retirement, a selection of what he would have.

clue.text: They're still abstracts

parts.note: abstract sculptures that, unlike Calder's mobiles, do not move

explanation.definitionFit: Calder's static sculptures were named in contrast to his moving mobiles.

clue.text: Leading man said to turn round and play the leading man in Salomeé

definitions.text: play the leading man in Salomeé

parts.note: a hero is the leading man of a story

indicators.note: to turn round tells us the word just before is read backwards

explanation.surface: An actor is told to spin round and take the lead role in Wilde's play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'play' here means toy with or manipulate: Herod's wife plays her husband, the leading man, getting the Baptist's head through her daughter's dance.
explanation.definitionFit: Herod's wife is the schemer in Wilde's and Strauss's Salomé who works on the king to gain her revenge.

clue.text: He was at pains in play, perhaps

definitions.text: He was at pains in play, perhaps

parts.words: He was at pains in play, perhaps
parts.note: someone at pains takes care, and Pinter's play is named for such a man, the odd-job keeper of a house

explanation.definitionFit: Pinter's 1960 play centres on a tramp offered a job looking after a building.

clue.text: Humorist canon to forbid pigmeat?

parts.note: to bar something is to forbid it
ham is cured pig meat

explanation.surface: A comic churchman is told to ban pork.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Harris Barham, a canon of St Paul's, wrote the comic Ingoldsby Legends.

clue.text: Medicine man produces false article

parts.note: sham means false or fake
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A healer is exposed as producing a fake object.
explanation.definitionFit: A tribal healer believed to work with spirits is the classic medicine man.

clue.text: Reserve denture to display 1A

definitions.note: an infinitive phrase standing for the noun: the thing used for showing the owner's Latin label

parts.note: to book is to reserve
a plate is a set of false teeth

explanation.surface: Someone books a set of false teeth to show off.
explanation.definitionFit: The ornamental label pasted inside a book's cover carries the owner's ex libris inscription.

clue.text: Quiet cupbearer as shepherdess

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
Hebe was cupbearer to the Greek gods

explanation.surface: A silent waitress serves as a country shepherdess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'as' is a nod to As You Like It, where the scornful shepherdess of this name appears.
explanation.definitionFit: In Shakespeare's As You Like It she is the shepherdess courted by Silvius.

clue.text: Moor at Dover landmark in Wuthering Heights ()

definitions.meaning: a moor is open uncultivated upland

definitions.text: at Dover landmark in Wuthering Heights
definitions.meaning: put beside a cliff, the famous Dover landmark, this word gives the name of Brontë's hero of Wuthering Heights

explanation.walkthrough: The White Cliffs of Dover are the landmark; joined to it, the word becomes the name Heathcliff.
explanation.definitionFit: Heathland is open moorland, and Heathcliff is the brooding hero of Emily Brontë's novel.

clue.text: End lie about 13's alma mater

indicators.note: about here means turned around or rearranged, so the letters before it are reordered

explanation.surface: Put an end to a lie about where an artist studied.
explanation.definitionFit: Rembrandt (13) enrolled at the university in this Dutch city, his birthplace.

clue.text: Embittered Miss whose house "was of old brick and dismal, and had a great many iron bars to it "

definitions.text: Embittered Miss whose house "was of old brick and dismal, and had a great many iron bars to it "

parts.words: Embittered Miss whose house "was of old brick and dismal, and had a great many iron bars to it "
parts.note: Pip's description of Satis House in Great Expectations, home of the jilted spinster

explanation.definitionFit: The jilted spinster of Great Expectations lives at Satis House, the gloomy barred mansion Pip describes.

clue.text: County associated with furze in novel

definitions.text: County associated with furze in novel

parts.words: County associated with furze in novel
parts.note: Sheila Kaye-Smith's 1916 novel pairs this southern English county with gorse, another name for furze

explanation.walkthrough: The novel is Sussex Gorse; furze and gorse are the same spiny shrub. Sussex is a county on England's south coast.
explanation.definitionFit: The south-coast English county gives half the title of Kaye-Smith's novel Sussex Gorse.

clue.text: Humorist whose gorge was rising

parts.note: S. J. ..., the American comic writer, published a 1961 collection called The Rising Gorge

explanation.definitionFit: The American humorist's collection The Rising Gorge puns on the phrase for mounting disgust.
